note: Shared citation list for education pages. Keys that also appear in rules.json swap_tags.citations or context_references use the same key and DOI. Every entry was checked against Crossref (DOI, authors, year, journal, volume, pages) and the finding against the abstract on 2026-10-21. Never add an entry without doing the same.

sato2021.authors: Sato S, Yoshida R, Kiyono R, et al.
sato2021.title: Elbow Joint Angles in Elbow Flexor Unilateral Resistance Exercise Training Determine Its Effects on Muscle Strength and Thickness of Trained and Non-trained Arms
sato2021.finding: Unilateral preacher curls trained only in the extended-elbow range (0-50 deg, long muscle length) grew the elbow flexors more than the same range in the flexed position (80-130 deg): 8.9% vs 3.4% muscle thickness in untrained adults over 5 weeks.
sato2021.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

wolf2023.authors: Wolf M, Androulakis-Korakakis P, Fisher J, Schoenfeld B, Steele J
wolf2023.title: Partial Vs Full Range of Motion Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
wolf2023.journal: International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
wolf2023.finding: Across studies, partial vs full range of motion made a trivial-to-small difference, with a possible edge for partials done at long muscle lengths. The effect is small and uncertain.
wolf2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

wolf2025.authors: Wolf M, Androulakis Korakakis P, Piñero A, et al.
wolf2025.title: Lengthened partial repetitions elicit similar muscular adaptations as full range of motion repetitions during resistance training in trained individuals
wolf2025.finding: In 30 trained people (one arm each way, 8 weeks, sets to failure), lengthened partials and full range gave similar elbow flexor and extensor growth. Programme included dumbbell and Bayesian curls, single-arm pulldowns and rows; lat size was not measured.
wolf2025.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

nunes2020.authors: Nunes JP, Jacinto JL, Ribeiro AS, et al.
nunes2020.title: Placing Greater Torque at Shorter or Longer Muscle Lengths? Effects of Cable vs. Barbell Preacher Curl Training on Muscular Strength and Hypertrophy in Young Adults
nunes2020.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
nunes2020.finding: Cable preacher curls (more tension near the top) and barbell preacher curls (more tension in the stretch) gave similar biceps growth.
nunes2020.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

maeo2021.authors: Maeo S, Huang M, Wu Y, et al.
maeo2021.title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths
maeo2021.finding: Seated leg curls (hamstrings at longer length) grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls.
maeo2021.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

pedrosa2022.authors: Pedrosa GF, Lima FV, Schoenfeld BJ, et al.
pedrosa2022.title: Partial range of motion training elicits favorable improvements in muscular adaptations when carried out at long muscle lengths
pedrosa2022.finding: Leg-extension partials in the long-length part of the range grew the quads more than partials in the short-length part.
pedrosa2022.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

kassiano2023.authors: Kassiano W, Costa B, Kunevaliki G, et al.
kassiano2023.title: Greater Gastrocnemius Muscle Hypertrophy After Partial Range of Motion Training Performed at Long Muscle Lengths
kassiano2023.finding: Calf-raise partials in the stretched range grew the gastrocnemius more than partials near the top.
kassiano2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

schoenfeld2017dose.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
schoenfeld2017dose.title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis
schoenfeld2017dose.finding: Meta-analysis of 15 studies: more weekly sets per muscle went with more growth (graded dose-response; 10+ sets largest).
schoenfeld2017dose.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

pelland2026.authors: Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Robinson ZP, Hinson SR, Zourdos MC
pelland2026.title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains
pelland2026.finding: Meta-regressions of 67 studies: growth keeps rising with weekly set volume, with diminishing returns; indirect sets fit best counted as half a set.
pelland2026.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

robinson2024.authors: Robinson ZP, Pelland JC, Remmert JF, et al.
robinson2024.title: Exploring the Dose–Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions
robinson2024.finding: Exploratory meta-regressions: muscle growth increased as sets were stopped closer to failure (estimated RIR); strength gains were similar across a wide range of RIR. The exact curve is uncertain.
robinson2024.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

refalo2023.authors: Refalo MC, Helms ER, Trexler ET, Hamilton DL, Fyfe JJ
refalo2023.title: Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
refalo2023.finding: Meta-analysis: training to momentary failure did not produce clearly more growth than stopping short of failure.
refalo2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

wackerhage2019.authors: Wackerhage H, Schoenfeld BJ, Hamilton DL, Lehti M, Hulmi JJ
wackerhage2019.title: Stimuli and sensors that initiate skeletal muscle hypertrophy following resistance exercise
wackerhage2019.finding: Review: mechanical signals (tension sensed by the muscle fibre) are the leading candidate trigger for resistance-training hypertrophy; metabolic stress and damage are less certain.
wackerhage2019.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

schoenfeld2017load.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
schoenfeld2017load.title: Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations Between Low- vs. High-Load Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
schoenfeld2017load.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
schoenfeld2017load.finding: Meta-analysis: low-load and high-load training gave similar growth when sets were taken to failure; heavy loads gave more strength.
schoenfeld2017load.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

damas2016.authors: Damas F, Phillips SM, Libardi CA, et al.
damas2016.title: Resistance training‐induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage
damas2016.finding: Early in a training programme, muscle protein synthesis was not linked to growth while damage was high; it only tracked growth once damage had faded.
damas2016.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

andersen2014.authors: Andersen V, Fimland MS, Wiik E, Skoglund A, Saeterbakken AH
andersen2014.title: Effects of Grip Width on Muscle Strength and Activation in the Lat Pull-Down
andersen2014.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
andersen2014.finding: EMG: narrow, medium and wide pronated lat-pulldown grips gave similar lat activation over the whole rep; the wide grip allowed about 4% less load.
andersen2014.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

lusk2010.authors: Lusk SJ, Hale BD, Russell DM
lusk2010.title: Grip Width and Forearm Orientation Effects on Muscle Activity During the Lat Pull-Down
lusk2010.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
lusk2010.finding: EMG: a pronated (overhand) pulldown grip gave slightly more lat activation than a supinated grip; grip width made no difference.
lusk2010.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

maeo2023.authors: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, et al.
maeo2023.title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position
maeo2023.finding: In 21 adults (one arm each way, 12 weeks), overhead cable elbow extensions grew the triceps long head 1.5-fold more than pushdown-position extensions (+28.5% vs +19.6%), and the lateral and medial heads 1.4-fold more, even though lighter loads were used.
maeo2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

kubo2019.authors: Kubo K, Ikebukuro T, Yata H
kubo2019.title: Effects of squat training with different depths on lower limb muscle volumes
kubo2019.finding: Full squats and half squats grew the knee extensors similarly (about 5%); neither grew the rectus femoris or hamstrings. Full squats grew the adductors (6.2% vs 2.7%) and glute max (6.7% vs 2.2%) more. MRI, 17 men, 10 weeks.
kubo2019.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

plotkin2023.authors: Plotkin DL, Rodas MA, Vigotsky AD, et al.
plotkin2023.title: Hip thrust and back squat training elicit similar gluteus muscle hypertrophy and transfer similarly to the deadlift
plotkin2023.finding: Set-equated hip thrust and back squat training grew the glute max similarly in untrained adults; squats grew the quads and adductors more; glute medius/minimus and hamstrings grew little in either. Higher glute EMG during hip thrusts did not predict more growth.
plotkin2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

kinoshita2023.authors: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, et al.
kinoshita2023.title: Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training
kinoshita2023.finding: Standing (knee straight) calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises (lateral 12.4% vs 1.7%, medial 9.2% vs 0.6%); soleus growth was similar (2.1% vs 2.9%). 14 untrained adults, 12 weeks.
kinoshita2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

haugen2023.authors: Haugen ME, Vårvik FT, Larsen S, et al.
haugen2023.title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance – a systematic review and meta-analysis
haugen2023.journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
haugen2023.finding: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth (no significant difference).
haugen2023.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

bourne2017.authors: Bourne MN, Duhig SJ, Timmins RG, et al.
bourne2017.title: Impact of the Nordic hamstring and hip extension exercises on hamstring architecture and morphology: implications for injury prevention
bourne2017.finding: Ten weeks of 45-degree hip extension grew the biceps femoris long head more than Nordic curls; both grew the semitendinosus; only hip extension grew the semimembranosus (MRI, 30 recreationally active men).
bourne2017.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

zabaletakorta2021.authors: Zabaleta-Korta A, Fernández-Peña E, Torres-Unda J, Garbisu-Hualde A, Santos-Concejero J
zabaletakorta2021.title: The role of exercise selection in regional Muscle Hypertrophy: A randomized controlled trial
zabaletakorta2021.finding: With equal volume and intensity, leg extensions grew all three measured regions of the rectus femoris, while Smith-machine squats grew only the middle of the vastus lateralis.
zabaletakorta2021.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

chaves2020.authors: Chaves SFN, Rocha-Júnior VA, Encarnação IGA, et al.
chaves2020.title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men
chaves2020.finding: Untrained men did flat, incline or combined bench press once a week for 8 weeks with equal sets. Strength gains were similar; at the upper-chest site (second intercostal space) muscle thickness grew most with the incline press. The other two sites did not differ.
chaves2020.verified: Crossref works API 2026-10-21 (DOI, title, journal, volume, issue; Crossref lists no authors) plus PubMed 32922646 for authors and pages 859-872; finding checked against the abstract

schoenfeld2016freq.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
schoenfeld2016freq.title: Effects of Resistance Training Frequency on Measures of Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
schoenfeld2016freq.finding: Ten studies, volume-equated: training a muscle twice a week gave more growth than once a week; three vs two times was unresolved.
schoenfeld2016freq.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

schoenfeld2019freq.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Krieger J
schoenfeld2019freq.title: How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency
schoenfeld2019freq.finding: Twenty-five studies: no significant difference in growth between higher and lower frequencies when weekly volume was equated; non-equated studies favoured higher frequency modestly, mostly through more volume.
schoenfeld2019freq.verified: Crossref works API, 2026-10-21 (authors, year, journal, volume, pages); finding checked against the abstract

kobayashi2026.authors: Kobayashi Y, Maeo S, Eihara Y, Ono M, Sato M, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T
kobayashi2026.title: Exercise-specific preferential hypertrophy of individual elbow flexor muscles after incline versus preacher dumbbell curl training
kobayashi2026.finding: 21 untrained adults, 12 weeks, one arm incline curl and the other preacher curl (MRI): biceps brachii grew more after incline (+22.1% vs +18.9%), brachialis and brachioradialis grew more after preacher; total elbow-flexor growth did not differ (+17.6% vs +19.2%). Heads of the biceps were not separated.
kobayashi2026.verified: Crossref works API and PubMed abstract (PMID 42829982), 2026-10-21; finding checked against the abstract. Published online 2026-10-04; volume and issue not yet assigned.
